observations.text: SP entered the Power on / ELP Stall with the briefed climb attitude and bank, but did not initiate recovery at the first indication of loss of A/C control, so the IP directed the recovery inputs and the level off was completed with 350 ft of altitude loss. Performance met the block requirement, which allows IP direction at this stage, but it was marginal for the Training Section. The trend across the two repetitions was positive, with the second entry flown closer to the Techniques and Procedures Manual sequence. Independent recovery initiation is expected to improve by the next sortie.

SP maintained the climb attitude and bank through the entry and initiated the recovery at the beginning of loss of A/C control after the IP's verbal prompt, without any intervention on the controls. Recognition of the stall cue was delayed, but the correction was applied correctly, the level off was completed with 300 ft of altitude loss and the exit heading was held at 10 degrees of deviation. No secondary stall appeared. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the entry with the briefed climb attitude and bank and initiated the recovery at the first indication of loss of A/C control without IP prompting. Minor errors in power and pitch coordination during the level off produced 200 ft of altitude loss and 15 knots of airspeed deviation, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. No secondary stall developed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the Power on / ELP Stall in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual, holding the climb attitude and the required bank up to the stall indication. Recovery was initiated promptly at the beginning of loss of A/C control and the A/C was leveled off with 90 ft of altitude loss, 6 knots of airspeed deviation and 3 degrees of exit heading deviation. No secondary stall appeared and no IP input was required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the Power on / ELP Stall with exceptional accuracy, holding the climb attitude and bank exactly as briefed and recovering at the first indication of loss of A/C control. The level off was completed with 40 ft of altitude loss, 3 knots of airspeed deviation and 1 degree of exit heading deviation, with no secondary stall and no IP input at any point. Performance was above the desired levels for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a delayed and insufficient forward stick input at the stall indication, did not initiate the recovery at the beginning of loss of A/C control as required by the Techniques and Procedures Manual. The nose was allowed to drop well below the horizon and a secondary stall appeared during the pull, with the result that the IP took the controls and completed the level off after 450 ft of altitude loss. The recovery sequence requires review before the next repetition.

SP, due to a startle response that displaced the memorised recovery sequence, did not apply the Techniques and Procedures Manual recovery actions in the correct order at the onset of loss of A/C control. Power and pitch inputs were reversed in sequence and the exit heading was allowed to diverge by 20 degrees, with the result that the IP directed the corrective inputs and executed part of the level off, which was completed with 400 ft of altitude loss. No secondary stall appeared after the IP's intervention.

SP maintained the climb attitude and bank through the entry and completed the Power on / ELP Stall recovery within the block requirement, but only after the IP's verbal prompt to unload and to check the power setting. Recognition of the initial loss of A/C control was late by approximately two seconds, and the level off was completed with 300 ft of altitude loss and 20 knots of airspeed deviation, at the limit of the allowed values. Marginal performance for the Training Section. The second repetition was flown with an earlier recovery initiation, and unprompted recognition of the stall cue is expected to improve.

SP executed the Power on / ELP Stall in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual and initiated the recovery at the beginning of loss of A/C control without any IP prompt. Minor errors in power management during the level off produced 180 ft of altitude loss and 14 knots of airspeed deviation, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention, and no secondary stall appeared. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP held the climb attitude and the required bank up to the stall indication and initiated the recovery promptly and accurately at the beginning of loss of A/C control. The A/C was leveled off with 110 ft of altitude loss, 7 knots of airspeed deviation and 4 degrees of exit heading deviation, with no secondary stall and without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the Power on / ELP Stall with accuracy above the desired standards, maintaining the climb attitude and bank precisely and recovering at the first perceptible stall cue. Altitude loss during the level off was held to 35 ft, airspeed deviation to 3 knots and exit heading deviation to 1 degree, with no secondary stall and no IP input. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an over-controlled pull during the level off, did not level the A/C off by losing the minimum altitude possible and allowed a secondary stall to appear. Proper action was not taken at the secondary stall indication, with the result that the IP took the controls, unloaded the A/C and completed the recovery after 500 ft of altitude loss and 30 knots of airspeed deviation. The recovery pull rate requires review against the Techniques and Procedures Manual before the next repetition.

SP, due to failure to recognise the undesired aircraft state before it developed further, did not initiate the recovery at the beginning of loss of A/C control and allowed the bank to increase past the briefed value during the entry. The exit heading diverged by 25 degrees and the level off was completed only after the IP directed the rudder and power inputs, with 480 ft of altitude loss. Recognition of the first departure cue is the limiting factor at this stage.

SP, due to an imprecise power reduction schedule during the recovery, did not level the A/C off by losing the minimum altitude possible and allowed the airspeed to build past the briefed recovery value. The deviation was recognized and corrected with delay, after the IP's verbal prompt, with the result of 300 ft of altitude loss and 20 knots of airspeed deviation at the limit of the allowed values. No IP intervention on the controls was required and no secondary stall appeared.

SP, due to an absent cross-check of aircraft state against the primary flight instruments after the stall break, did not hold the exit parameters called for by the Techniques and Procedures Manual during the level off. Exit heading deviation reached 10 degrees and altitude loss reached 300 ft, both at the limit of the allowed values, and both were corrected only after the IP called them out. The recovery was completed without IP intervention on the controls, but recognition was delayed throughout.

SP executed the Power on / ELP Stall within the desired standards, maintaining the climb attitude and bank up to the stall indication and initiating the recovery without IP prompting. Minor errors in pitch capture during the level off produced 280 ft of altitude loss and 18 knots of airspeed deviation, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention, but close to the upper edge of the allowed band. Marginal performance for the Training Section. Both repetitions showed the same tendency to delay the level off, and tighter altitude control is expected to improve with further practice.

SP executed the Power on / ELP Stall in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual, holding the climb attitude and the required bank and recovering promptly at the beginning of loss of A/C control. The A/C was leveled off with 120 ft of altitude loss, 8 knots of airspeed deviation and 4 degrees of exit heading deviation, with no secondary stall and no IP input. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the Power on / ELP Stall with exceptional accuracy, entering with the briefed climb attitude and bank and recovering at the first stall cue with no wasted control input. Altitude loss during the level off was held to 45 ft, airspeed deviation to 4 knots and exit heading deviation to 2 degrees, with no secondary stall and no IP prompt at any stage. Performance was above the desired levels for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a nose-high entry flown above the briefed climb attitude with the bank left uncorrected, did not execute the maneuver in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual and did not initiate the recovery at the beginning of loss of A/C control. A secondary stall appeared during the level off and proper action was not taken, with the result that the IP took the controls and completed the recovery after 550 ft of altitude loss and 35 knots of airspeed deviation. The entry attitude and the recovery sequence require review before the next repetition.

SP, due to the startle effect at the onset of the departure from controlled flight, did not apply the memorised recovery sequence and hesitated before the first control input. The A/C was allowed to diverge 30 degrees from the exit heading and the level off was completed only after the IP directed and executed part of the recovery, with 500 ft of altitude loss. Anticipation of the stall cue during the entry is expected to reduce the initial hesitation.

SP, due to an under-controlled recovery with insufficient forward stick to break the stall, did not level the A/C off by losing the minimum altitude possible. The deviation was recognized and corrected with delay, only after the IP's verbal prompt to unload, with the result of 300 ft of altitude loss and 10 degrees of exit heading deviation at the limit of the allowed values. No IP intervention on the controls was required and no secondary stall appeared.

SP, due to stress that narrowed the scan to the pitch attitude alone, did not monitor airspeed and heading through the recovery and did not hold the exit parameters called for by the Techniques and Procedures Manual. Airspeed deviation reached 20 knots and exit heading deviation reached 10 degrees, both at the limit of the allowed values, and both were corrected only after the IP called them out. The recovery itself was completed by SP without IP intervention on the controls.

SP, due to a slightly late power reduction at the stall break, did not level the A/C off by losing the minimum altitude possible. The error was minor and was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention, with the result of 210 ft of altitude loss and 13 knots of airspeed deviation. No secondary stall appeared and the exit heading was held within 7 degrees of deviation.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during a critical phase of flight, did not maintain the climb attitude and bank steadily before the stall indication. The recovery was initiated correctly at the beginning of loss of A/C control, but the level off was flown with 250 ft of altitude loss and 9 degrees of exit heading deviation, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. No secondary stall appeared.

SP executed the Power on / ELP Stall in accordance with the Techniques and Procedures Manual, maintained the climb attitude and bank and initiated the recovery promptly at the beginning of loss of A/C control. The level off was completed with 140 ft of altitude loss and 9 knots of airspeed deviation, inside the desired values but close to their upper edge on both repetitions. Marginal performance for the Training Section. The tendency to delay the pitch capture by approximately one second was consistent, and tighter altitude control during the level off is expected to improve.

SP executed the Power on / ELP Stall with exceptional accuracy, holding the briefed climb attitude and bank up to the stall indication and initiating the recovery at the first perceptible cue with no wasted control input. The A/C was leveled off with 40 ft of altitude loss, 3 knots of airspeed deviation and 1 degree of exit heading deviation, with no secondary stall and no IP prompt or intervention at any point. Control precision was above the desired levels for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.
